about.note: The Town of Bartlett, Carroll County, covers the villages of Bartlett, Glen, part of Intervale and the Attitash area. It is run by a three-member Board of Selectmen with a Town Administrator, and voters decide the budget at the annual Town Meeting in March. Selectmen, Planning Board and ZBA minutes come from the town's Agenda Center; ten sets of Selectmen minutes (March 18 to October 21, 2026) were read for this record. Minutes for the May to July Selectmen meetings were not opened. The 2026 budget and Town Meeting results are posted only as Adobe cloud links that could not be opened, so the budget block is mostly empty. Water service in parts of town comes from separate water precincts with their own tax rates. Plain-English summaries written by AI; items with needs_review=true are uncertain.

issues.title: Property tax bills now come twice a year; a town-wide revaluation is planned for 2027
issues.status: First half-year bill went out in June 2026 (due July 1); the second 2026 bill comes after the state sets the 2026 tax rate
issues.next: November or December 2026: second 2026 tax bill, due 30 days after the bill date
issues.summary: Bartlett used to send one property tax bill a year. The Selectmen switched to two bills a year because interest on tax anticipation notes (short-term loans the town takes out to pay bills until taxes come in) went up over the past two years. Separately, the board chair said the town will revalue all property in 2027.
points: The June 2026 bill was half of the 2025 tax rate applied to the 2025 assessment, due July 1, 2026.
The second bill uses the 2026 assessment and the 2026 rate, minus what was paid in June.
The last single bill (2025 taxes) was mailed December 12, 2025 and was due January 14, 2026.
Bartlett's 2025 rate was $6.02 per $1,000 before any water precinct tax, up from $5.58 in 2024 (state tax rate tables).
March 18, 2026: Chair Chandler said the town will do a town-wide revaluation in 2027. Abatement requests (asking the town to lower an assessment) must be filed each year.

issues.title: Proposed gravel pit off Route 16
issues.status: Before the Planning Board; listed for its September 10 public hearing (result not yet posted)
issues.summary: St. Pete LLC wants to dig and sell gravel from about 20 acres off Route 16 over ten years, leaving a flat lot of about 9 acres for future commercial use. Planning Board members disagree on whether Bartlett's zoning allows a new gravel pit at all, and the board asked for legal advice.
points: About 600,000 cubic yards in total, roughly 60,000 a year for 10 years, across two lots (Tax Map 2RT16-1 Lot 057L01 and Tax Map 2RT302-1R Lot 017R00). Crushing about once a year.

Would need a state commercial driveway permit onto Route 16 and state alteration of terrain (large earth-moving) and shoreline permits; no wetland impacts expected, per the applicant's engineer (Verdantas).

July 6: several board members said gravel pits were historically not allowed except grandfathered ones. The applicant said the Selectmen view it as allowed under the zoning ordinance's general provisions (Section N); the board said that view does not bind it and asked the NH Municipal Association for an opinion.

Aug 3: the town attorney had answered one of two questions. If the Planning Board denies it, the applicant can go to the Zoning Board of Adjustment; if the ZBA approves, it returns for an excavation permit.
Several residents asked about the proposal at the August 3 meeting; the chair said the board would respond publicly as the process moves forward.

issues.title: Master Plan update, and whether to plan for AI data centers
issues.status: Planning Board revising the 2016 Master Plan; data centers still under discussion
issues.next: 2026-11-02: Planning Board public hearing (agenda posted; contents not reviewed)
issues.summary: The Planning Board is updating the town's Master Plan (the long-range plan that guides zoning; the current one was finalized April 19, 2016). It is also debating whether the plan should address AI and data centers, including whether to allow them and on what terms.
points: Aug 26: the board needs updated sections from the Road Agent and the Fire Department; Fire and Roads were preparing them (Aug 3).
July 6: the chair polled members on putting a question on the town ballot to ban data centers; the board said it was too soon.
Members raised energy and water use, on-site power and small nuclear units, and whether Bartlett would benefit from the jobs.
June 8: the ZBA noted the update needs technical changes and new sewer service boundaries; public input is welcome after the draft update.
Aug 3: the board discussed warrant article and public hearing deadlines for the March 2027 Town Meeting.

issues.title: Flood protection on the Saco River: the Dugway berm and federal grants
issues.status: Town's Flood Hazard Mitigation Committee seeking a new design and FEMA grant money
issues.summary: A town committee wants to rebuild flood protection at the Dugway berm on the upper Saco River using FEMA's BRIC program (Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities, federal money for projects that reduce disaster damage). There is no current design, and the Selectmen want cost estimates before any engineering spending.
points: April 15: BRIC money is available again after the 2025 program was ended; the town must reapply (July deadline). The engineer previously involved declined the project. The town has also applied for BRIC money for a Razor Brook bridge project.
April 15: the Selectmen adopted the town's Hazard Mitigation Plan, prepared by Mapping and Planning Solutions.
Sept 24: estimates from HEB Engineering were received; a committee member said a BRIC grant decision was expected by year-end.

Oct 21: the board agreed the committee may use HEB's grant writer only if there is no charge, with any estimates sent to the Selectmen's office first. Committee members proposed a warrant article for a flood reserve fund.
Selectman Munro said the last major flood was in December 2023 (April 29 meeting).

issues.title: Where the school buses park in winter
issues.status: Draft agreement between the town, a private landowner and the Bartlett School District still under negotiation
issues.next: 2026-11-10: Bartlett School Board meeting (per the Oct 21 Selectmen minutes)
issues.summary: The school district's buses have parked at Town Hall, but the Selectmen say there is no room and the buses get in the way of snow removal and highway equipment. The school district and town are working on a memorandum of understanding (MOU, a written agreement) to park them on private land nearby instead.
points: Aug 11: the School Board liaison reported a possible winter spot on private land, if the Highway Department plows it; bus drivers also want steep roads such as Glen Ledge plowed by 6 to 6:30 AM.
Oct 7: the Selectmen asked to drop the draft's lighting and insurance clauses; the landowner offered the lot at will with a termination clause.
Oct 21: the school side cited a gravel quote of about $3,000; Chair Chandler said the school would pay only for gravel, with the Highway Department doing the labor and upkeep.
Two of the district's four buses need to be plugged in during winter.
The school's Facilities Committee is also looking at parking near the school.

attendance_note: Counts the ten sets of Selectmen minutes opened (March 18, April 1, 15 and 29, August 11 and 26, September 9 and 24, October 7 and 21, 2026), all after the March 10 town election. Minutes for the May to July meetings were not opened, so these are not full-term totals. Munro arrived late on October 7 and 21 and is counted present.

budget.departmentsNote: Bartlett votes its budget at the annual Town Meeting in March. The 2026 budget, 2026 warrant and 2025 annual report are posted on the Selectmen's page only as Adobe cloud links, which could not be opened for this research, so the operating budget, prior-year figure and department amounts are not shown.
drivers: Interest on tax anticipation notes (short-term borrowing until taxes come in) rose over the past two years, which led to twice-a-year tax bills starting in 2026.
Town Meeting set up a $100,000 capital reserve fund for town upgrades (year not stated in the minutes); none had been spent as of October 21, 2026.
From January 1, 2027, the town will pay half of health and dental premiums for part-time employees working 20 to 39 hours a week.
A replacement John Deere 710 backhoe was leased in March 2026 with no 2026 cost; a 2027 warrant article will ask voters to continue the lease.

revenue.note: The state's 2025 tax table shows a total 2025 commitment (all property taxes billed for town, schools, state education and county) of $13,007,436 on a valuation of $2,084,269,125. The town's own revenue estimate form was not found.

taxRate.rateLabel: 2025 tax year, Lower Bartlett Water Precinct
taxRate.note: Dollars per $1,000 of assessed value. Every Bartlett property pays the same base rate ($6.02 in 2025: town $1.36, local school $2.61, state education $1.21, county $0.84). Property in the Lower Bartlett Water Precinct also paid the precinct's $1.37, for $7.39. Property outside a precinct paid $6.02; the Bartlett Village Water Precinct rate was not found. The 2026 rate had not been set as of October 31, 2026.
